cards.title: Find the same exact decomposition with less repeated work
cards.use: You analyze small Boolean truth vectors and need a canonical factor artifact, not just a yes/no answer.
cards.mechanism: Share one matrix layout per partition, rank exact candidate descriptors, then strictly validate and reconstruct only the leading candidates.
cards.takeaway: C40's 20-case confirmation gives a 3.95× internal analysis speedup; C39's 19 public cones give 3.46×. Both select the same best artifact as the exhaustive control.
cards.boundary: Best means best within the bounded partition set and four artifact families. The implementation admits at most 10 variables. C40 is development-blind in source-family selection, on one host. This is not a comparison with ABC or a new general decomposition theorem; corpus redistribution remains unresolved.

cards.title: Make packed Boolean input construction cheaper
cards.use: You really need the complete Boolean answer vector and spend substantial time building its input masks.
cards.mechanism: Construct repeating packed masks efficiently before evaluating the expression. The shared constructor also benefits direct BitSet and common-subexpression elimination (CSE).
cards.takeaway: A selected fresh 18-variable confirmation case drops from 14.03 ms to 1.33 ms for cold public packed-CM evaluation.
cards.boundary: This is an old/current implementation ablation, not a CM-versus-native claim or an aggregate across all cases. The full output still has 2^n bits; warm gains are smaller and some paths regress.

metrics.scope: Windows; fresh synthetic confirmation; all seven backend paths

cards.title: Reuse positional masks across renamed inputs
cards.use: Repeated requests share a variable count and order but use different variable names.
cards.mechanism: A bounded positional cache can reuse the same masks without treating every renamed basis as a new allocation.
cards.takeaway: On the selected renamed-input trace, cold q32 time falls from 30.36 ms with named LRU caching to 1.49 ms with positional caching.
cards.boundary: The warm named-LRU result is faster here (0.47 versus 0.58 ms). Memory bounds, eviction and request shape decide whether this helps; no universal cache policy was promoted.

metrics.scope: Linux EPYC 7702P; consumed portability panel; 2 MiB cache / 64 KiB pressure case

cards.title: Deliver a full truth vector without keeping it all resident
cards.use: A file or downstream process needs every output bit, but peak memory and first delivery matter.
cards.mechanism: Evaluate and deliver chunks with the same ordering and file obligations as the complete-output control.
cards.takeaway: For the selected 24-variable cold file output, 32 KiB chunks take 32.17 ms versus 160.79 ms for complete packed output. A separate memory diagnostic reports 48.37 versus 147.34 MiB process peaks.
cards.boundary: Timing and memory were measured on different Linux hosts and must not be combined into one run. This still writes the complete exponential-size answer; small chunks and warm batches can regress. Tune against the real reader and durability contract.

cards.title: Count XOR-constrained solutions without enumerating assignments
cards.use: Your constraints are affine equations over GF(2), as in coding matrices or parity checks.
cards.mechanism: Use elimination and rank to count the solutions; indexed rows reduce repeated work under conditioning.
cards.takeaway: On one public 1,800-variable matrix and eight queries, indexed Python takes 28.96 ms versus 103.91 ms for the original Python implementation. Indexed M4RI takes 41.43 ms on the same host and schedule.
cards.boundary: This is a structured counting algorithm and implementation result, not a generic CM representation advantage. It does not handle arbitrary nonlinear CNF. One matrix cannot establish a general Python-over-native ranking.

metrics.scope: Linux EPYC 7713; eight public coding matrices and fresh n1024/n2048 controls

cards.title: Count overlapping CNF factors with exact arrays
cards.use: You need exact full-CNF counts for a problem whose elimination width fits a bounded plan.
cards.mechanism: Bucket elimination combines local factors. Object-dtype NumPy arrays accelerate the larger factors while preserving Python-integer exactness.
cards.takeaway: On the public printer model and eight queries, arrays take 29.76 ms versus 121.17 ms for Python min-fill. Natural-order CUDD takes 4.66 ms on this same case.
cards.boundary: This example improves the Python control but loses to natural-order CUDD. Arrays lose on many narrow factors, and high-width plans explicitly refuse. Full assignments and distinct projected assignments require different counting contracts.

metrics.scope: Linux EPYC 9654; all 35 final-panel cases; q1/q8; nine paired repetitions

cards.title: Keep large BDD counts exact in Python
cards.use: You already hold a CUDD BDD and need an exact integer when floating-point rounding or overflow is unacceptable.
cards.mechanism: The dd 0.6.0 prototype calls Cudd_ApaCountMinterm, converts its binary digits to a Python integer, and frees the native allocation in finally.
cards.takeaway: On OR-of-64 padded to 128 variables, native APA takes 12.60 µs versus 113.16 µs for Python exact traversal. The existing double call takes 11.13 µs but rounds this result.
cards.boundary: A local binding prototype, not an upstream dd release or a new counting algorithm. About 9–10× faster than Python on the three larger tested diagrams; trivial roots favor Python. Construction is excluded. A 1,100-variable padded literal overflows the double control. Allocation-failure injection remains untested.

cards.title: Separate a faster kernel from a slower public call
cards.use: You repeatedly evaluate a prepared full relation and can measure preparation, evaluation and delivery separately.
cards.mechanism: CM compilation can reduce kernel work, but public wrappers and preparation can consume the saving. Compare the same evaluator and delivered output.
cards.takeaway: The September 15 symmetric replay puts the bare CM/CSE-flat time ratio near 0.91 on both Windows and Linux: about 9% less kernel time. The public wrapper instead costs about 3.7–3.9× the CSE-flat time.
cards.boundary: Kernel-only gains are not end-to-end gains. Reuse break-even varies by formula and host; many formulas never amortize preparation versus CSE-flat. The matched biology pilot found no demonstrated CM-specific session advantage.

selection: Curated useful mechanisms, not a global leaderboard. Numeric examples are selected disclosed cases, not estimates of typical user speedup. Ratios in the cards are control time divided by candidate time unless explicitly labelled otherwise.

article.title: An exact winner, with less work validating losing candidates
article.recommendation: Best-supported software-note candidate: the bounded C16 decomposition workflow.
article.reason: The output contract is explicit, the selected artifact is preserved, C39/C40 extend the evidence, and C41 tests individual mechanisms. This supports an engineering article about exact software design and measured tradeoffs.
article.limits: The internal exhaustive control is the comparator. ABC's fixed 4-LUT ACD output has a different objective. A task-equivalent external comparison, redistributable replay inputs and a completed prior-art review would strengthen a research submission. Novelty and publication acceptance are not established.
article.secondary: A practical Python/CUDD article is also useful: exact integer counts, rounding examples, safe allocation cleanup and resident-root benchmarks. Credit CUDD's existing arbitrary-precision algorithm; the contribution here is the binding and evaluation.

stops.title: Cut fusion: keep it experimental
stops.text: The frozen q64 whole-session gate measured only 0.493× speedup against CSE, below its 1.10× requirement. Exact outputs alone did not make the optimization worthwhile.

stops.title: Native batching: a completed no-go
stops.text: The prospective q96 gate reached about 1.078×, below its frozen 1.10× materiality requirement. No learned router or production default was promoted.

stops.title: Do not reuse the historical SymPy headline
stops.text: The historical approximately 76× observation timed unlike tasks. Supplied-row evaluation, a full truth table, SAT, counting and expression simplification need separate comparisons.
